The last day to request an absentee ballot is October 20, 2026 . Apply early for an absentee ballot for the upcoming 2026 General Election. Voted ballots must be received by the Clerk’s Office or a secure drop box by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day (November 3, 2026) . Election Day Voting – Tue., Nov 3, 2026 Mail-In Ballot Info Online Mail-In Application Overseas Voters Request a Mail-In Ballot /* Reset theme-injected icons */ .button-help::before, .button-help::after, .button-action::before, .button-action::after { content: none !important; display: none !important; background: none !important; width: 0 !important; height: 0 !important; } /* Help button (optional secondary style if you ever need it) */ .button-help { transition: background-color .3s ease, color .3s ease; display:inline-block; padding:12px 16px; background:#f4f4f4; border:1px solid #1c5363; border-radius:4px; text-decoration:none; color:#1c5363; font-size:1rem; line-height:1.35; } .button-help:hover { background:#d6e6f2!important; color:#1c5363!important; cursor:pointer; } /* Primary call-to-action button (orange, no icons) */ .button-action { float:none !important; clear:both !important; display:block !important; box-sizing:border-box; margin:1rem auto !important; padding:14px 24px !important; max-width:360px; width:100%; background:#cd744d !important; border:none !important; border-radius:6px !important; color:#ffffff !important; font-weight:600; font-size:1.05rem; line-height:1.35 !important; text-align:center; text-decoration:none !important; white-space:normal !important; word-break:normal; overflow-wrap:anywhere; } .button-action:hover { background:#fa8557 !important; color:#ffffff !important; } Candidate Information Looking for candidate and campaign information? Visit the New Mexico Secretary of State’s Candidate & Campaigns webpage. Want to know your districts? Use Find My District in the Voter Portal. Important Dates Sept 22, 2026 - Notice of Election with Voting Locations gets mailed Oct 6, 2026 – Last day to submit online voter registration. Oct 6, 2026 – Early voting begins at the Santa Fe County Clerk’s Office. Oct 6, 2026 – Absentee (mail-in) ballots begin mailing to voters who have requested them. Oct 12, 2026 – Polls are closed for Indigenous People's Day. Oct 17, 2026 – Expanded early voting begins at additional early voting locations throughout the county. Oct 20, 2026 – Last day to request an absentee (mail-in) ballot (must be received by this date). Oct 31, 2026 – Last day of early voting at expanded early voting locations. Nov 3, 2026 – Election Day (Polls open 7:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m.). Same Day Voter Registration is available during early voting and on Election Day at voting locations. Helpful Resources NM SOS Voting & Elections Voter Portal On the Ballot Races on the ballot vary by voter district in the General Election. The list below reflects the offices Santa Fe County voters may see on their ballot. The easiest way to view your exact ballot and candidates is to use the New Mexico Secretary of State’s Candidate Portal. Who is on the Ballot Federal Offices U.S. Senator U.S. Representative – District 1 U.S. Representative – District 2 U.S. Representative – District 3 Statewide Offices Governor Lieutenant Governor Secretary of State Attorney General State Auditor State Treasurer Commissioner of Public Lands Court of Appeals Judge – Position 1 State & District Offices (varies by district) New Mexico House of Representatives – Districts 41, 43, 45, 46, 47, 48, 50 1st Judicial District Judge – Divisions 4 & 8 (unexpired term) Santa Fe County Offices Magistrate Judge – Divisions 1, 2, 3, 4 County Sheriff County Assessor County Commissioner – District 1 County Commissioner – District 3 Probate Judge Ballot Questions and Constitutional Amendments Read them here Not sure which districts you live in? We've updated our district maps. District Maps Some contests are district-based, meaning not every voter will see the same races. Real-Time Voter Turnout Tracker Track voter participation during the 2026 General Election using Santa Fe County's real-time turnout dashboard. Turnout data includes in-person early voting and absentee ballots processed by the Clerk's Office. Data is updated regularly throughout the election period. Open in new window Turnout Command Center View detailed turnout information by jurisdiction, voting method, and party. Reporting is delayed by approximately one hour. Open in new window Note: Turnout trackers are informational and may not reflect final turnout until all eligible ballots have been processed.
